analysis: All changed files in this batch are test files under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Engine/. No production source is included, so no runtime security control changes here. Tests reference production behavior that likely changed elsewhere (not supplied): the encoded body ingress bound is now NemotronSuperServingPolicy.maximumEncodedBodyBytes (previously 8 MiB), encodedHeaderQuote charges bodyBytes*32 + templateBytes*4 + 16 MiB, and the failure is now Failure.bodyTooLarge, which maps to media_too_large. The video charge bound rose from 3,751,221,756 to 4,875,295,228 bytes (NemotronSuperVideoBindingTests.swift line 168 on head). New NemotronSuperOpenRouterVideoTests.swift covers ingress, inspection, per-frame decode and the budget refund after serving. It reads committed clips from the source tree and verifies their SHA-256 before use. Nothing in the tests is itself risky, and the fixtures are public. A test at line 112 asserts that ingress plus plan total stays within the video media charge. The tests also assert that budget reservations return to baseline after success, cancellation and rejection, and that concurrent requests get a busy rejection. This covers the availability and DoS surface of the bounds (T-010, T-029). Remaining questions for integration or the production-code pass: (1) the larger ingress bound and larger video charge raise memory exposure on the provider. Reviewers should confirm in production source that the header quote is claimed against GlobalKVCacheBudget before the body is parsed or decoded, and that the 32x multiplier is conservative. (2) The tests expect bodyTooLarge to map to code mediaTooLarge with statusCode 400, while the comment says 413 at the coordinator. The coordinator mapping is outside this scope. (3) Video decode runs on untrusted container data, which is parser attack surface (AVFoundation). This is covered by the production decode path, not these tests. No concrete regression is identifiable from tests alone.
